final_trade_decision:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is a staged accumulation, not a market order. Take only a 25% starter near 180.38 (if AMZN is already held, hold the core and take no starter add), reserve 40% for the 177.10–178.35 VWMA/10-EMA confluence with partials into 176.82 and 173.30–173.52, and release the final 35% only on a daily close above 181.70 with volume >=45M shares AND a positive MACD histogram. Size the aggregate so a slide from average cost to the 171.47 close-based stop costs no more than ~1.5% of portfolio value; if that forces a smaller than standard position, accept the smaller size rather than widening the stop. Full-position invalidation is a close below 165.74.

**Investment Thesis**: The bull wins the part of the debate that determines long-horizon returns: four consecutive quarters of accelerating revenue (9.4% -> 10.8% -> 12.6% -> 13.9%) on a ~$575B base, operating income roughly tripled ($12.2B -> $36.9B), record 6.4% operating margin beating the 2020 peak, record 47.0% gross margin, FCF swinging ~+$49B from -$16.9B to +$32.2B at 1.06x net income, and a genuinely repaired balance sheet (current ratio 0.94x -> 1.05x, cash +36% to $73.4B, liabilities/equity 2.17x -> 1.61x). The primary trend confirms it: 180.38 > 10 EMA 178.35 > 50 SMA 170.51 > 200 SMA 145.58, all rising, with ascending March lows 171.47 -> 179.26 and price above a rising VWMA of 177.10. Critically the bear conceded the fundamentals outright ("the 10-K is real... I accept the data") and offered only a price/timing objection, which cannot support a Sell or Underweight against a compounding business. The bear is nonetheless right that reward-for-risk at 180.38 is mediocre: new 2024 closing high, +23.9% above the 200 SMA and +5.8% above the 50 SMA, only ~1.3% to the 181.70 ceiling versus 3-5% to support; the 3/28 high pierced the upper Bollinger band (181.70 vs 181.51) and closed back inside; March volume ~36M versus 45-50M+ in February; MACD still bearish-crossed (2.547 vs 2.599, histogram -0.053); RSI 61.90 against February peaks of 73.78/72.43 is a mild negative divergence; ATR of 3.26 can cut both the 10 EMA and VWMA in one session; and macro (10Y 4.20% with a March high ~4.34%, CPI +3.09%, Fed on hold, Mag 7 rotation, Neutral 5.1 sentiment on one of three sources) adds a multiple headwind. Sequencing risk is real too: ~87% of FY2023 FCF landed in Q4, the capex cut (-17.2% to $52.7B) is the exhaustible half of the FCF story, 400bps of margin expansion is not repeatable, and H2'24 laps 7.8% operating-margin comps. None of that breaks the thesis - it argues against paying up in the 179.26-181.70 noise band, which is exactly why the stance is Overweight rather than Buy and why the Trader's 25/40/35 tranche structure, 171.47 stop and 186-188 / 197.7 measured-move profit zones are affirmed as written. The one tightening: the 35% breakout tranche stays unfunded unless both the >=45M volume and positive MACD histogram confirm. What would change the call: a failed breakout (rejection at 181.70 on >=45M volume and a close back below 177.10); a 10Y decisively above 4.34%; a weak Q1'24 FCF print accompanied by commentary implying the Q4 FCF concentration was not seasonal (a weak headline alone is expected seasonality and should not be sold); or arriving valuation data showing a clear premium to history without matching earnings revisions. Explicit gaps I am not papering over: no valuation multiples, no insider-transaction data, no AWS/advertising segment data, and a 1-of-3 sentiment read. No risk-management debate was conducted for AMZN; the Trader's proposal was assessed directly against the research plan and evidence.

**Price Target**: 187.0

**Time Horizon**: 6-12 months (first scale-out 186-188; full measured move ~197.7)
